spec_doc.description: The written spec (path added by the diffs).

coverage_map.description: EVERY subsystem-contract invariant mapped to the red law that verifies it: each {invariant_id, test_name, test_file, kind, drives, plant}. Each entry names what the law DRIVES and the PLANT: the production defect that must turn it red. Behavioural by default; structural only with a reason.

kind.description: behavioural: the law CALLS the production code named in `drives` and asserts on what it does. structural: the law reads source or configuration (a manifest, a link map, a grant list) because the invariant IS a property of the text. A law about behaviour sealed as structural is the defect this field exists to stop: laws that read source for a token, called a stand-in, or built their own copy of the thing they guarded passed their seal and stayed green under planted defects in the call sites they claimed to guard.

drives.description: The production symbol the law invokes, with its file (e.g. 'createRegistry(...).validate — src/registry.ts'). For kind=structural, the file or artefact read.

plant.description: The one smallest edit to PRODUCTION code (not to the test) that must turn this law RED (e.g. 'drop the ...conditional spread from effective() in src/registry.ts'). If no production edit can turn the law red, it is not guarding production.

plant_observed.description: What the drafter SAW when it applied the plant and ran the law: the failing assertion, verbatim. Planted, observed, reverted before sealing. The drafter's claim: the engine validates its shape, not its truth.

structural_reason.description: Required when kind=structural: why no behavioural law can express this invariant.

testing_method.description: The axiomatic/property-based approach + engine used (e.g. fast-check property tests), grounded in method_findings.

uncovered.description: Contract invariants with no red test — MUST be empty.

laws.description: The RED laws, BY ADDRESS (contract-records-by-address-v1). A seat supplies {path, commit}: where the committed law file is. The ENGINE stamps, at seal, from RunDeps.tree_root: blob_sha (git rev-parse <commit>:<path>) and tests (the it/test titles in that blob, in file order). A reviewing seat reads the exact law with `git show <commit>:<path>` and checks it against blob_sha. No patch body is ever model output: gig c1771b13's attester hit the 32,000 output-token cap three times re-typing ~150KB of patches into the retired `diffs` field.

blob_sha.description: engine-stamped at seal; a seat-supplied value that disagrees with git is refused (law_bytes_mismatch)

tests.description: engine-stamped at seal: the it/test titles in the blob, in file order
